To address these issues, we propose SCAFNet, a Semantic Compensated Adaptive Fusion Network, featuring three core components: 1) The Semantic Compensation Module (SCM) that aligns local-global features via cross-attention to resolve spatial-semantic mismatches; 2) The CNN-Transformer Feature Adaptive Fusion (CTFAF) module improving feature integration by dynamically balancing the local details of CNN and the global context of Transformer through cross-branch attention interactions and dynamic parameterization; 3) The Change Feature Identification Module (CFIM) computing channel and spatial weights, enhancing true changes while suppressing disturbances such as seasonal variations. Experiments on CDD and WHU-CD datasets demonstrate SCAFNet’s superior robustness and accuracy, outperforming existing methods through effective feature fusion. The source code and supplementary materials will be made available at https://github.com/Gyroprime/SCAFNet.

title: GAENet: A Global Attention-Aware Enhanced Network for Remote Sensing Target Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Due to the large-scale variation of targets and complex background in optical remote sensing images, existing remote sensing target detection algorithms face significant challenges. To address these issues, a global attention-aware enhanced network (GAENet) for remote sensing target detection is proposed. Firstly, the convolution and attention fusion module (CAFM) is introduced in the backbone network, which effectively combines the convolution and attention mechanism modules in feature modeling, enhancing the long-distance dependency between features and the feature expression ability of local regions. Secondly, the dynamic detection head (Dyhead) is introduced, which adaptively adjusts the attention distribution to improve the model’s perception ability for targets of different scales. Experimental results on the DIOR dataset show that the proposed method can significantly improve the detection accuracy of multi-scale targets in complex scenes, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The source code is available at https://github.com/object-detection/GAENet.

title: New Accuracy Indicators for Assessing ICESat-2 Photon Cloud Filtering in Forested Areas
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Accurate photon cloud filtering is a critical preprocessing step for deriving forest parameters from ICESat-2 data. As filtering quality directly affects the reliability of subsequent applications, selecting an appropriate filtering method for a forest area is essential. Therefore, it is necessary to objectively and accurately evaluate filtering performance before further applying ICESat-2 data. However, conventional filtering accuracy indicators such as recall, precision, and F-score often fall short in objectively reflecting filtering performance, as they do not adequately capture the preservation of ground and canopy photons, nor the resulting terrain and canopy height accuracy. To address these limitations, this study proposed four new filtering accuracy indicators tailored to forest environments: Ground Signal Retention Rate (GSRR), Ground Noise Residual Rate (GNRR), Canopy Signal Retention Rate (CSRR), and Canopy Noise Residual Rate (CNRR). These indicators enable a more detailed and application-oriented evaluation of filtering performance across both ground and canopy layers. Five commonly used filtering algorithms were assessed across six representative test datasets with varying canopy cover and terrain complexity. Experimental results show that the proposed indicators exhibit a strong and statistically significant correlation with terrain RMSE, withGSRRachieving a correlation coefficient of −0.93 and ap-value below 0.001, whereas the conventional indicators exhibit absolute correlation coefficients below 0.40 andp-values greater than 0.05.

title: FSA-SARNet: A Frequency-Guided Semantic Segmentation Network for Remote Sensing SAR Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image semantic segmentation is crucial for all-weather, high-precision land-cover mapping. However, existing segmentation methods have limited performance due to their inability to resist well the speckle noise inherent in SAR images and neglecting the importance of frequency domain information. In this letter, we propose FSA-SARNet, a lightweight encoder-decoder network based on Frequency-Guided Attention. The main innovations of our method are as follows: (1) We design a Log-domain Guided Denoising Module (LGDM) to denoise by transforming the multiplicative speckle noise to additive noise. (2) We design a Frequency-Guided Spatial Attention Module (FGSA) to enable frequency-domain features to guide spatial-domain feature learning. (3) We introduce dynamic upsampling for the decoder to recover feature map details. Evaluated on the FUSAR-Map and WHU-OPT-SAR datasets, our method delivers superior performance and efficiency, achieving competitive MIoU scores of 42.67% and 47.00% with a compact model size of only 7.03M parameters.

title: DEM Super-Resolution Using Frequency-Selective Cross Attention Assisted by Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Digital Elevation Model (DEM) plays a crucial role in geospatial analysis. However, high-resolution DEM is often costly to acquire and has limited spatial coverage. This letter proposes a DEM super-resolution method that integrates auxiliary information from remote sensing image (RSI): dual-branch bidirectional feature guidance network (DBFGN). The proposed method adopts the Swin Transformer as the backbone and incorporates a channel-spatial joint Transformer (CSJT) module to enhance both global and local feature extraction capabilities. To effectively extract consistent texture from RSI that strongly correlates with elevation variations, we design a mutual-guided network (MGN) based on frequency-selective cross-attention (FSCA), enabling adaptive extraction and fusion of high-frequency structure. Experiments conducted on the Swiss and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing DEM and general image super-resolution methods in the challenging 8× upscaling task of DEM super-resolution, achieving RMSE and MAE of 3.108 m and 1.818 m, respectively. Compared to the second-best method, our approach improves accuracy by 8.37%, validating its effectiveness in complex height reconstruction tasks.

title: Multiscale Dynamic Graph Network for Forecasting of Wind Speeds in Offshore Regions
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Accurate prediction of wind speed in offshore areas is critical to maintaining the reliability and stability of offshore wind power. However, existing graph neural network methods focus only on a single time scale and ignore potential temporal patterns. Moreover, they rely on predefined graph structures and cannot capture dynamic spatial correlations between ocean locations, which affects the representation of offshore wind speed patterns. Therefore, we introduce the Multi-Scale Dynamic Graph Network (MSDGN) to enhance wind speed forecasting accuracy in offshore regions. MSDGN introduces a network with a multi-scale pyramid structure to capture potential time-based dependencies in raw data across various scales, and infers spatial relationships between oceanic locations at specific scales through a self-adapting learning graph network. Subsequently, the proposed temporal graph network with multi-scale concurrently captures both the time-based dependencies in sequence data and the spatial relationships among oceanic locations. Finally, the model integrates a scale-wise fusion module to facilitate cooperation among various scales, further enhancing prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on Chinese sea data show our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in multi-node wind speed prediction.

title: FAPMNet: Flow-Aligned Prototype Memory Network for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) in bi-temporal remote sensing images aims to localize and semantically classify changed regions, which is crucial for land cover monitoring and disaster assessment. Existing methods often struggle with spatial misalignment and semantic inconsistency between temporal domains. In this letter, we propose FAPMNet, a Flow-Aligned Prototype Memory Network, which integrates a Mamba-based Vision State Space Model (VSSM) encoder for efficient long-range spatial modeling. To address temporal misalignment, a Flow Alignment Module (FAM) estimates dense flow fields to warp and align features. A Prototype Memory Module (PMM) further enhances semantic consistency via class-guided feature reconstruction. Evaluated on the SECOND and Landsat-SCD datasets, FAPMNet achieves new state-of-the-art results with 74.48% mIoU and 66.04%Fscdon SECOND, and 90.04% mIoU and 90.20%Fscdon Landsat-SCD, surpassing recent Transformer and Mamba-based baselines.

title: DCFI-Net: Dual-Branch Cross-Frequency Interaction Diffusion Model for Remote Sensing Image Shadow Removal
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Diffusion-based shadow removal methods have demonstrated impressive results on natural images, but face challenges such as high computational cost and content distortion when dealing with remote sensing images. To address these limitations, a dual-branch cross-frequency interaction diffusion model DCFI-Net for shadow removal in remote sensing images is proposed. In DCFI-Net, the diffusion process is transferred to the wavelet domain to reduce computational cost. Within the wavelet-based diffusion framework, two parallel dedicated branches for the low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) components are proposed. Then, a cross-frequency interaction module (CFIM) is utilized to facilitate the information exchange between these two branches, which guides the synergistic network optimization. Finally, we propose a feature preserving module (FPM) to mitigate the scene discrepancies between the shadow and shadow-free images. The experimental results conducted on the UAV-SC and SRGTA datasets demonstrate that DCFI-Net significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both the reconstruction and perceptual quality. Notably, DCFI-Net exhibits substantial advantages in precisely reconstructing edge details and preserving scene consistency, which are crucial for remote sensing image analysis.

title: Acoustic-to-Seismic Signal Attenuation and Aircraft Trajectory Tracking
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Airborne sound sources generate strong pressure disturbances that couple with the ground to produce acoustic-to-seismic signals, leaving a continuous seismic footprint detectable by sensors. This study simulates the seismic response of moving aircraft using the Finite Difference Method and analyzes the relationship between signal amplitude and the distance to the flight path. By integrating the wavefront diffusion equation with the distance formula, we derive a mathematical link between maximum amplitude and trajectory parameters. Based on this relation, an inversion algorithm using linear array data is developed for trajectory tracking. Field data from Beijing Capital International Airport validate the feasibility of the method. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach enables reliable large-scale and long-term aircraft monitoring, complementing traditional radar and acoustic technologies for aviation surveillance.

title: FGANet: Fuzzy-Embedded Semantic Decoupling Network for Sea–Land Segmentation in Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Sea-Land Segmentation (SLS) of remote sensing imagery plays a vital role in coastal change analysis, intelligent ocean development, and marine resource management. However, it still faces numerous challenges, such as the difficulty in segmenting narrow waterways, spectral similarity between land and sea, and uncertainty in sea-land boundaries. To effectively overcome these challenges, we propose a fuzzy-embedded semantic information decoupling network (FGANet). First, we design a contrast-driven fusion module (CDFA) that guides multi-level feature fusion through decoupled deep features, enabling precise sea-land discrimination. Second, we develop a global prior guided fusion module (GPM) to reduce misclassification in spectrally similar regions. Finally, we introduce a fuzzy connection (FC) unit that mitigates uncertainty at the sea-land boundary through a two-dimensional Gaussian blurring approach. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on publicly available SLSD and SLBD datasets, with results confirming that the proposed FGANet outperforms other advanced existing approaches in the field.

title: A Practical Landsat-9 Land Surface Temperature Sharpen Method Combining Top-of-Atmosphere Multispectral and Panchromatic Reflectance
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The thermal infrared (TIR) band of the Landsat-9 satellite has a spatial resolution of 100 meters, which is coarser than the optical multispectral bands of the 30-meter resolution and the panchromatic band of the 15-meter resolution. Existing image fusion algorithm studies primarily focuses on multispectral and panchromatic bands. For the TIR band with the lowest spatial resolution, although Landsat-9 land surface temperature (LST) products are resampled to 30m using the Cubic algorithm to match the multispectral bands, the physical mechanism of sharpening methods remains unclear, and they fail to fully leverage the higher spatial resolution advantage provided by the panchromatic band. This study proposes a practical LST sharpening method (TOA-MsPS) by integrating the correlation between top-of-atmosphere TIR brightness temperature (BT) and the fused reflectance of Multispectral and Panchromatic bands. The TOA-MsPS method comprises three steps: panchromatic and multispectral band fusion, correlation modeling of reflectance and BT, and LST end-to-end retrieval. Compared to existing methods, the TOA-MsPS method sharpens the spatial resolution of both TIR band BT images to 15 m without relying on external parameters, simultaneously deriving the LST data. All input data for the method consists of remote sensing observations at the TOA, reducing external parameter uncertainties and error propagation inherent in the preprocessing steps of current LST retrieval algorithms, such as atmospheric correction, resampling, and emissivity estimation. Qualitative visual interpretation based on visual inspection indicate that TOA-MsPS derived LST images exhibit significantly enhanced detail and reasonable local spatial distribution. Quantitative validations using ground site measurements demonstrate that the sharpened LST images achieve comparable accuracy to Landsat-9 LST products while substantially improving spatial resolution, with root mean square errors of 2.45K (LST product) and 2.35K (LST sharpen), respectively. Furthermore, the TOA-MsPS method can be directly applied to remote sensing data from multiple other remote sensing data sources, further enhancing the precision of long-term land surface thermal radiance monitoring.

title: Spatial-Frequency Joint Learning Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, as a crucial research direction in remote sensing, aims to achieve pixel-wise land cover classification by leveraging the abundant spectral and spatial information of HSI. However, existing approaches direct their primary attention to spectral-spatial feature analysis while neglecting to explore latent properties in the frequency domain. To solve this issue, we put forward a spatial-frequency joint learning Mamba (SFMamba) framework for HSI classification. Its core component is the Wavelet Mamba Block (WMB), which adopts a dual-branch design with spatial and frequency branches. In the spatial branch, we utilize convolutional layers for spatial domain feature extraction. In the frequency branch, we use wavelet transform to decompose input features into a low-frequency component together with three high-frequency components. The low-frequency component is processed by a convolutional block, while the high-frequency components are modeled by a Mamba block, achieving effective learning of both local and global representations in the frequency domain. Experimental results on two public datasets show that SFMamba outperforms several existing classification methods, demonstrating its effectiveness. Specifically, SFMamba achieves overall accuracies of 98.92% on the ZY1-02D Huanghekou (ZYHHK) dataset and 99.03% on the WHU-Hi-LongKou (LongKou) dataset. Our code is available at: https://github.com/zhe-meng/SFMamba.

title: Improving the Spatial Representation of Reservoir Evaporation Using SAR-Based Wind Fields
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Evaporation losses from reservoirs can be substantial, yet spatial variability in evaporation rates is difficult to quantify, in part due to the difficulty of estimating high-resolution wind fields at the water-air interface. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers a promising approach to estimate high-resolution wind fields over lakes. To test the utility of SAR-based winds to improve spatial representation of reservoir evaporation, we developed a framework fusing Sentinel-1 based wind fields with gridded meteorological estimates of air temperature, humidity, and solar radiation to estimate distributed evaporation rates at Lake Mead, USA using the Penman open water evaporation equation. We validated outputs at over-water buoys and benchmarked the results against wind and evaporation estimates derived solely from the Real-Time Mesoscale Analysis (RTMA) data product. Sentinel-1 wind field accuracy matched or outperformed RTMA, with a wind direction mean absolute error (MAE) of 41.3° compared to 40.3° and a wind speed MAE of 1.3 m/s compared to 1.8 m/s. This framework yielded a 25x increase in spatial resolution of wind fields (100 m) and evaporation (100 m) compared to RTMA-alone (2500 m), enabling identification of greater spatial variability across Lake Mead than was previously possible. This framework could be used globally for high-resolution evaporation mapping to support water resources monitoring, modeling, and management.

title: Hybrid Integration of CNN and Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Multispectral Image Super-Resolution
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: This letter proposes KAN-MSI-SR (KMSR), a novel deep learning framework for multispectral image super-resolution that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). The model employs a KAN-Block to enhance nonlinear spectral-spatial representation, combined with CNNs for local feature extraction. Supported by channel weighting, residual connections, and global skip links, the approach effectively improves reconstruction accuracy and spectral consistency. Experiments on Sentinel-2 imagery demonstrate that KMSR outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, providing a robust and efficient solution for Multispectral imagery (MSI) super-resolution.

title: Incidence Angle Optimization for Formation-Flying Across-Track SAR Interferometry
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Single-pass across-track synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interferometry using formation flying is a well-established technique for the generation of high-quality digital elevation models (DEMs), as it avoids temporal decorrelation and allows for long baselines, thus leading to high height accuracy. A successful implementation, employed in the TanDEM-X mission, foresees the use of a Helix formation, which entails a reduced control effort to be maintained in the presence of external perturbations. However, an intrinsic limitation of the Helix concept lies in the inherently time-varying baseline and height of ambiguity (HoA), which results in non-homogeneous DEM performance. This letter proposes an analytical method to minimize the HoA variability at the global level by optimizing the range of incidence angles used at each latitude. The approach is primarily aimed at systems, such as TanDEM-X, for which the area to be imaged becomes significantly smaller than the ground access range as the latitude increases. A two-step approach is presented: An initial approximate solution is derived in closed form and subsequently refined. The method is validated against numerical results and compared with simpler strategies involving fixed incidence angles, showing reduced variation of the HoA for different formation parameters. The procedure presented in this work could enable a better operation of current interferometric SAR systems and foster an improved design of future ones.

title: Relationship Between Wave-Related Reynolds Number and Doppler Velocity at Grazing Incidence
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: We show empirical evidence that the mean spatial gradient of the Doppler velocity, measured by a coherent X-band marine radar at grazing incidence, serves as a reliable proxy for measuring the so-called wave-related Reynolds number - defined as the product of air-side friction velocity and significant wave height divided by the kinematic viscosity of the surface water. Comparisons to approximately 180 hours of in situ observations spanning various environmental conditions in the Southern North Sea yield an overall squared correlation coefficient of 0.93, and a normalized root-mean-square error of 16%. These results suggest that coherent marine radar offers a practical and relatively cost-efficient tool for observing key parameters related to ocean surface dynamics and air-sea interactions, such as whitecap coverage.

title: RARM-YOLO: Remote Sensing Small-Target Detection Model Enhanced by Dual-Branch Region-Aware Refinement Module
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Remote sensing image object detection is characterized by dim features of small objects and complex backgrounds. In most networks, simply enhancing small object features may disrupt global consistency and affect detection results. This paper designs a region-aware refinement module to locate the enhanced target semantic representation and suppress background noise interference, and a dual detection branch to fuse underlying details and shallow semantic features at the neck of the feature pyramid, enhancing the model’s ability to focus on very small targets. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves an mAP50% of 76.0% on the VEDAI dataset, which is 10.6% higher than the original YOLOv8s. The mAP50-95% is 46.5%, which is 7% higher. The precision and recall rates are improved by 7.5% and 12.2% respectively. The generalization performance was verified on VisDrone2019 and SODA-A remote sensing datasets, with mAP50% of 47.1% and 73.8% respectively, a model size of only 29.5MB, balancing lightweight and high detection performance. This method provides a technical approach involving the cooperative optimisation of multiple modules for target detection in complex remote sensing scenes, offering significant application value.

title: A Multitask Collaborative Learning Approach for Fine-Grained Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Fine-grained object detection in remote sensing images is challenged by high intra-class variation and low inter-class distinction, as well as optimization inconsistency between classification and localization tasks. To address these, we propose MCLNet, a Multi-Task Collaborative Learning Network. MCLNet is a dual-stream architecture that integrates fine-grained classification with coarse-grained detection to improve detection accuracy. To enhance oriented localization, we treat all fine-grained objects as coarse-grained ones during training, which expands the dataset and improves the accuracy of oriented localization in the coarse-grained detection stream. Besides, we introduce a Coarse-to-Fine Hierarchical Constraint Mechanism (CHCM) that uses coarse-grained predictions as priors to guide fine-grained learning, enhancing both intra-class and inter-class feature representations. Additionally, we employ a Progressive Multi-Task Optimization Strategy (PMOS) that gradually trains the model to balance classification and localization tasks, reducing task interference. Extensive experiments on widely used benchmark datasets validate that MCLNet outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in fine-grained object detection.

title: LGRI: A Multimodal Image Registration Method Integrating Adaptive Log-Gabor Filtering With Rotation-Invariant Descriptors
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Multimodal image registration aims to accurately align images with differences in spatial structure or optical characteristics, serving as a key technology in remote sensing image processing and analysis. Currently, most registration methods are designed only for single-modal or limited cross-modal scenarios, often leading to distortions, artifacts, and registration errors when processing multimodal data. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal remote sensing image registration method called LGRI (Log-Gabor Rotation-Invariant), which integrates adaptive Log-Gabor feature extraction with rotation-invariant local binary descriptors. Specifically, we first design an adaptive Log-Gabor Structural-Frequency Detector (LGSFD) to extract highly repeatable and discriminative cross-modal feature points by leveraging spatial structure and frequency response. Then, we propose a Rotation-Invariant Noise-Robust Local Binary Descriptor (RINR-LBD), which improves robustness via arc-segment mean smoothing and ensures descriptor consistency through principal direction normalization. Finally, we refine the matches using Fast Sample Consensus (FSC) to effectively eliminate mismatches and improve registration accuracy. Experimental results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both the average number of correct matches and the matching success rate.

title: DA-PhysDiff: A Dual-Aware Physics-Informed Diffusion Model for SAR Image Despeckling
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Deep learning-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) despeckling faces two key challenges: physical model mismatch, where simplified noise assumptions fail to capture speckle’s statistics, and architectural generality, where standard networks struggle to separate noise from texture. To address this, we propose DA-PhysDiff, a dual-aware physics-informed diffusion model for SAR image despeckling. The proposed LogGamma-based stochastic differential equation models multiplicative speckle more accurately, while the dual-aware network composed of a Statistics-Conditioned Gamma Attention (SCGA) and a Frequency-Refined Adaptive Wavelet Convolution (FRA-WTConv) enhances both distribution and frequency awareness. Experiments on HRSID, MiniSAR, and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that DA-PhysDiff achieves up to +2.5 dB PSNR and +4.8% EPD-ROA improvement over recent diffusion models, while reducing parameters by 19% compared with SAR-DDPM and maintaining real-time inference.

title: The New Technology for Soil Moisture Measurement Based on GNSS-S Radar
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Soil moisture is a key variable governing land–atmosphere water and energy exchanges. This letter proposes a novel soil moisture retrieval technique based on GNSS-S (Global Navigation Satellite System–Scattering) radar. Unlike conventional GNSS-R systems that are restricted to specular reflection points, the proposed GNSS-S radar exploits distributed GNSS backscattering to enable continuous bistatic imaging of surface soil moisture. The system is mounted on an airborne or spaceborne platform and uses navigation satellites as illuminators of opportunity. GNSS-S imaging is achieved through signal-level preprocessing, backprojection-based image formation, geometric correction, and relative radiometric calibration. Airborne experiments demonstrate that continuous surface imaging with a spatial resolution of approximately 100 m × 100 m can be achieved using L-band GNSS signals. Comparative analysis with in-situ soil moisture measurements shows consistent spatial distribution trends, and quantitative evaluation reveals moderate to strong correlations depending on bistatic geometry. These results validate the feasibility of GNSS-S radar for area-wide soil moisture monitoring and highlight its potential as a complementary technique to conventional active SAR systems.

title: Four-Component Polarimetric Decomposition Method for High-Resolution PolSAR Vehicle Targets Based on Extended Scattering Models
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Polarimetric target decomposition is fundamental for interpreting scattering mechanisms in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery. However, existing model-based methods often overestimate volume scattering, exhibit coupling between surface and double-bounce components, and yield unstable results on high-resolution airborne data, particularly for man-made vehicle targets, hindering accurate characterization. This letter proposes a novel four-component decomposition method designed for high-resolution airborne PolSAR imagery. Building upon the classical modeling of volume and helix scattering, two physically extended components are incorporated: an extended surface scattering model and an extended double-bounce scattering model. The former employs a rotated dipole to describe surface polarization anisotropy beyond ideal single-bounce assumptions, while the latter incorporates a rotated quarter-wave mechanism to characterize amplitude–phase inconsistencies neglected in conventional dihedral models. Experiments on a high-resolution Ku-band vehicle dataset demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses volume overestimation, alleviates surface–double-bounce coupling, and enhances component stability while preserving edge and structural fidelity. The model achieves improved adaptability to complex targets without increasing component dimensionality, while maintaining strong physical interpretability, offering a new pathway for refined vehicle scattering analysis in airborne PolSAR data.

title: Automatic Coseismic Landslide Mapping by Integrating Classification and Change Detection Techniques
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Automatic co-seismic landslide mapping plays a crucial role in rapidly assessing post-disaster impacts and supporting emergency response efforts. However, most remote sensing-based approaches depend on either classification or change detection alone, failing to fully exploit their complementary strengths and thus limiting mapping accuracy. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel co-seismic landslide mapping approach that integrates classification and change detection techniques. The proposed approach consists of two main stages: automatic landslide sample generation and classifier-based mapping, both integrating classification and change detection. Specifically, in the first stage, sample reliability is improved by combining coarse change detection using pre- and post-event images with coarse classification based on the post-event image. In the second stage, classification and change detection results are fused using a maximum class probability decision strategy to further enhance mapping accuracy. Experiments conducted on two datasets covering the Mainling area in China and the Hokkaido region in Japan demonstrate that the proposed method achieved superior performance compared with existing approaches.

title: Unveiling Spectral Attention Redundancy With Explainable AI
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification has advanced significantly through transformer-based models that leverage self-attention (SA) to capture global spectral dependencies. However, most existing HSI transformers implicitly assume that SA provides a faithful and discriminative modeling of spectral information, an assumption that has rarely been examined. We examine SA behavior in HSI classification using adversarial perturbations guided by explainable AI (XAI) techniques. By comparing transformer attention distributions with Integrated Gradients (IG) importance scores, we uncover discrepancies between attended bands and decision-driving features. Experiments show that SA often forms redundant clusters across neighboring spectral bands and that attention patterns evolve across layers, shifting from a localized to a broader focus. Such redundancy improves robustness to spectral corruptions but reduces feature specificity and leads to repeated processing of highly similar bands, increasing computational burden. Our findings question the everyday use of raw attention as an explanatory clue and guide the design of more reliable and interpretable attention mechanisms for HSI.

title: Large-Scale Forest Height Estimation With TanDEM-X InSAR and Sparse LiDAR Based on LSC and Block Adjustment Model
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: The TanDEM-X bistatic Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) system has great potential for forest height estimation. However, single-polarization InSAR data cannot support a uniquely determined inversion of classical physical models due to insufficient observational information. Simplified models make inversion possible using only interferometric coherence amplitude, at the cost of reduced performance by uncertain semi-empirical parameters and a loss of adaptivity to variations in local forest properties. To address this issue, this letter proposes a framework based on a semi-empirical physical model, block adjustment model, and the least-squares collocation (LSC) method. The framework utilizes sparse spaceborne LiDAR canopy height as a reference and selects tie points in overlapping areas to establish constraints, enabling robust estimation of semi-empirical model parameters on a large scale. Subsequently, variance-covariance estimation is employed to develop an LSC-based local calibration method, mitigating residual inversion errors caused by variations in forest attributes and terrain slope within local areas. Validation at two test sites in the USA and Spain shows that, compared to the results obtained from the SINC model and semi-empirical model inversions, the proposed framework improves accuracy by more than 32% and 21%, respectively, highlighting its potential for large-scale forest height mapping with TanDEM-X InSAR and sparse LiDAR data.

title: UniMGS: Unsupervised Multimodal Guided Segmentation for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Generating pixel-level annotations for the semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images is labor-intensive and time-consuming. To address this issue, numerous studies attempt to generate pixel-level annotations through automatic or semi-automatic labeling strategies. However, due to the inherent complexity of remote sensing imagery and the presence of unseen classes, achieving both accurate foreground segmentation and precise class labeling remains highly challenging. In this paper, we propose an Unsupervised Multimodal Guided Segmentation (UniMGS) framework that generates pseudo-labels for remote sensing images without requiring any ground-truth annotations or additional prompts. Specifically, We propose a Mask Purification Module (MPM) that refines class-agnostic segmentation masks by applying an area filter and a ring-merging strategy to remove noisy masks and merge over-segmented regions. To assign precise categories to class-agnostic segmentation masks, we propose a Text-Driven Classifier (TDC) module. This module constructs an intra-class maximum spanning tree from a similarity matrix and incorporates cluster size constraints together with a confidence scoring mechanism, ultimately achieving precise class labeling. Experimental results on multiple remote sensing datasets demonstrate that UniMGS outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Our source code is available at https://github.com/nanwang0511/UniMGS.

title: Local-Motion Mamba With Frequency-Guided for Moving Infrared Small Target Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Moving Infrared Small Target Detection (MISTD) remains challenging due to the large computational load caused by multi-frame input and background motion interference, leading to poor real-time and accuracy performance. To address these issues, we propose STLMamba, a spatial-temporal framework that integrates long-range dependency modeling with local feature sensitivity, guided by infrared video and frequency priors. Specifically, an Adaptive Multi-directional Frequency Enhancement (AMFE) module exploits spatial frequency cues to enhance targets, while an Efficient Local-motion Mamba (ELM) with a learnable Local Dynamic Gaussian Motion (LDGM) mechanism captures motion patterns and suppresses background noise. Experiments demonstrate that STLMamba achieves 43.14 FPS in NUDT-MIRSDT and 49.22 FPS in TSIRMT, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: DCTNet: Integrating Deformable Convolution and Transformer-Based Feature Fusion for High-Performance SAR Ship Detection
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)–based ship detection has become an indispensable technique for applications in maritime surveillance, oceanic defense systems, and marine resource assessment. However, factors such as speckle noise, sea clutter, and the diversity of ship scales severely restrict the robustness and accuracy of detection. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a one-stage detection network, termed DCTNet, which integrates a Deformable Convolution-based Multi-scale Fusion (DCMF) module and a Transformer-enhanced Feature Pyramid Aggregation Network (TFPAN). The DCMF module employs deformable convolution and channel partitioning to adaptively capture multi-scale features, thereby enhancing the representation of small-scale or low-contrast ships while effectively suppressing background interference. The TFPAN module incorporates Transformer attention mechanisms with progressive feature aggregation to strengthen multi-scale feature interaction and semantic consistency. In addition, a Triple Feature Fusion (TFF) strategy is designed to preserve local details and ensure global context transmission, effectively mitigating the loss of small target features during the fusion process. Experimental results on the SAR-Ship-Dataset and HRSID demonstrate that the proposed DCTNet achieves excellent performance and exhibits strong generalization ability.

title: SRAW-Attack: Space-Reweighted Adversarial Warping Attack for SAR Target Recognition
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery exhibits intrinsic information sparsity due to its unique electromagnetic scattering mechanism. Despite the widespread adoption of deep neural network (DNN)-based SAR automatic target recognition (SAR-ATR) systems, they remain vulnerable to adversarial examples and tend to over-rely on background regions, leading to degraded adversarial robustness. Existing adversarial attacks for SAR-ATR often require visually perceptible distortions to achieve effective performance, thereby necessitating an attack method that balances effectiveness and stealthiness. In this paper, a novel attack method termed Space-Reweighted Adversarial Warping (SRAW) is proposed, which generates adversarial examples through optimized spatial deformation with reweighted budgets across foreground and background regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SRAW significantly degrades the performance of state-of-the-art SAR-ATR models and consistently outperforms existing methods in terms of imperceptibility and adversarial transferability. Code is made available at https://github.com/boremycin/SAR-ATR-TransAttack.
